Petroleum Industrial & Civil Construction JSC Launches New Modular Construction Solution in Vietnam

HANOI, June 14 – Petroleum Industrial & Civil Construction JSC unveiled a new modular construction solution on Friday, aiming to boost efficiency and reduce project timelines in Vietnam’s rapidly expanding engineering and construction sector.

The company, one of the country’s established players in infrastructure and industrial project development, presented its Precast Modular System at a launch event in Ho Chi Minh City. The system is designed to streamline the assembly of oil and gas facilities, warehouses, and commercial buildings, amid rising demand for faster and more sustainable construction methods.

“We believe the Precast Modular System sets a new benchmark for quality, speed, and environmental responsibility,” said Nguyen Van Loi, General Director of Petroleum Industrial & Civil Construction JSC. “With this technology, we can shorten project delivery by up to 30% compared to traditional techniques, without compromising on safety or durability.”

The launch comes as Vietnam’s construction industry is projected to grow 8% this year, according to the Vietnam Engineering & Construction Association, driven by public infrastructure spending and foreign investment in manufacturing. Modular construction methods, which involve prefabricating building components off-site before rapid assembly, have gained traction in recent years as developers seek to minimize labor needs and material waste.

Tran Thi Bich, a senior analyst at AsiaBuild Research, said the move aligns with global trends. “Vietnam is catching up with advanced construction technologies. Modular systems can help address skilled labor shortages while meeting tight project deadlines in industrial zones and urban developments,” she noted.

Petroleum Industrial & Civil Construction JSC will initially deploy the system in its ongoing refinery and logistics projects, with plans to offer it to third-party developers later this year. Company representatives also cited potential applications in residential and educational facilities, as the government pushes for modernization in public infrastructure.

The company said it expects the modular solution to improve cost control and reduce construction-related emissions. “We are committed to supporting Vietnam’s sustainable growth,” Nguyen added. “This launch is a step forward for both our company and the industry.”
